fact_rationales.F10: The striking peripheral palisading arrangement and microcyst formation are more commonly seen in certain types of cervical carcinomas, but are not exclusive to any one candidate.
fact_rationales.F13: The hyperchromatic nuclei with minimal nuclear atypia are more typical of certain types of cervical carcinomas, but are not strongly indicative of any one candidate.
fact_rationales.F17: The strong, diffuse cellular membrane staining of the tumor cells with EMA is more commonly seen in certain types of cervical carcinomas, and is moderately supportive of adenocarcinoma and adenoid basal carcinoma.
fact_rationales.F9: The presence of cellular proliferations in the cervical stroma is more typical of malignant lesions, but the specific characteristics are not strongly indicative of any one candidate.
